title: Performance Data from the NIST Net-Zero Energy Residential Test Facility and official checksum inventory
version: Journal of Research of NIST volume 122 article 14; portal inventory retrieved 2026-08-11
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology

license.name: United States government work; NIST data portal describes the data as open and free

units.indoor_relative_humidity: unit field is blank in the downloaded metadata and must be resolved before analysis
units.airflow: cubic metre per hour or source channel unit
units.hourly_aggregation: Average, Hour value, or Sum as declared per metadata channel

measurement_uncertainty.description: The registered publication and channel metadata do not provide channel-level measurement uncertainties suitable for weighted calibration.

known_gaps: The Year 1 calibration measurement files and Year 2 holdout measurement files have not been downloaded or registered; this record is source metadata only.

The current Year 2 Metadata-hour.csv download is 65,632 bytes with SHA-256 d960162aa5120397da4f33180066815406ffa8808fbef40bcac3bdd74f89b631, but the official hashes.csv inventory lists 69,048 bytes and SHA-256 ac271b8c0267e00147c7c11e962c1be4a845be598d7b8a4c44ab62103dafadd4.

Timestamp timezone, daylight-saving convention, and interval labeling must be verified from the measurement files before alignment; America/New_York records the facility location policy, not a proven CSV timestamp encoding.
The publication reports 98.5 percent and 98.8 percent annual minute coverage for Years 1 and 2, respectively, and warns that missing values use NA while erroneous zero readings may remain.
Known operational anomalies include multi-day data-acquisition gaps and Year 2 changes to dehumidification equipment, ventilation scheduling, and thermostat configuration.
No canonical NZERTF building geometry, envelope, system representation, calibration parameter set, objective weights, or acceptance thresholds are frozen yet.

The registered Load-minute.csv raw file is only the first 2,097,152 HTTP bytes, not the full 367,266,298-byte official object; the official inventory records full-file SHA-256 0889a768e04994fc403aa2b13e2787b536144f158155f37a12f5f64ad6c7600c.

Source timestamps jitter and later contain acquisition gaps. The derived 900-record fixture retains source_timestamp and creates a separate one-minute canonical timestamp from the contiguous sequence counter.
Virtual-occupant flags prescribe a simulated family and are suitable for execution/attribution verification, not validation of natural human stochasticity.

preprocessing.description: Verify the NIST publication, official dataset checksum inventory, required hourly channel files, Year 1 calibration/Year 2 blind split, and the frozen Year 2 metadata checksum discrepancy.
Extract the first 900 pre-gap Year 1 load records, retain raw timestamps, normalize the one-minute clock, and map four virtual occupants plus appliance and lighting flags.

permitted_use.purpose: Calibration protocol design, later empirical validation, and deterministic verification of the prescribed virtual-occupant load schedule
permitted_use.notes: Keep source bytes under ignored raw storage. The compact derived schedule fixture contains selected U.S. government data fields. Do not register a calibration result until measurement files, uncertainties, exclusions, model inputs, and parameter bounds are frozen.
